memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'No one is to approach any close relative to have sexual relations. I am the LORD. Do not dishonour your father by having sexual relations with your mother. She is your mother; do not have relations with her. Do not have sexual relations with your father's wife; that would dishonour your father.'" - Lev 18:6-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here begins the longest section of the chapter, and its purpose is protection.

In the ancient world, a household was a place where power ran downhill. The head of the family had enormous authority over wives, children, servants, and dependants. In many cultures, that authority extended to their bodies. There was no one to appeal to.

God draws a line straight through that. The family must be safe.

Think about who these laws protect. Not the powerful. The daughter. The stepdaughter. The vulnerable young woman with nowhere to go and no one to tell. God legislates on behalf of people who had no voice.

That is worth remembering when we imagine the Bible as harsh towards the weak. Long before anyone had language for safeguarding, God was writing it into law.

And if you have suffered what these verses forbid — please hear this. God's word here is on your side. The wrong done to you was a violation of His command, and the guilt belongs entirely to the person who did it. Never to you. Jesus reserved some of His strongest words for those who harm the vulnerable (Matt 18:6).

If you carry this, please tell someone you trust. You were never meant to carry it alone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does it change your view of these laws to see them as protection?
2. Is your home a genuinely safe place for everyone in it?
3. Is there something you have carried alone that you need to tell someone?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You defend those who cannot defend themselves. Where there has been harm, bring healing and justice, and make our homes places of safety. Amen.
